sources.title: bitsandbytes 0.50.2 on PyPI

sources.title: 4-bit quantization API documentation
sources.date_basis: The page gives no publication date.
supports: Linear4bit defaults to compressed statistics, FP4, and uint8 storage.
The documented loading example quantizes through a device transfer.
limitations: The main documentation changes over time. Its CUDA example does not certify TPU transfer.

sources.title: Package import and backend discovery
sources.date_basis: Repository snapshot commit date; not the last modification date of each file.
supports: Package import loads and calls bitsandbytes.backends entry points.
The declared device set does not include xla.
The source package version is 0.50.3.dev0.
limitations: Plugin discovery does not prove TPU execution or supported device transfer.

sources.title: Operator schemas and fake implementations
sources.date_basis: Repository snapshot commit date; not the last modification date of each file.
supports: NF4 and blockwise operations have existing schemas.
The dequantize_blockwise.out schema returns no tensor.
GEMM accepts optional nested scale codes, map, and offset.
limitations: Fake implementations supply structural behavior. They do not execute device kernels.

sources.title: Params4bit and Linear4bit module source
sources.date_basis: Repository snapshot commit date; not the last modification date of each file.
supports: Unquantized device transfer calls _quantize and assigns packed output to self.data.
Linear4bit creates frozen base weights and saves QuantState components.
from_prequantized creates a parameter subclass on the selected device.
limitations: Source construction does not prove XLA compatibility.
The module defines saving but no matching _load_from_state_dict override for quantized state.

sources.title: Functional quantization and QuantState
sources.date_basis: Repository snapshot commit date; not the last modification date of each file.
supports: Compressed NF4 subtracts mean scale and quantizes centered scales in blocks of 256.
The second quantizer uses a signed dynamic map.
QuantState supports packed and unpacked dictionaries, with nested fields.
limitations: Serialization extracts the offset scalar. Metadata conversion includes host operations.

sources.title: Default Python operations and CUDA NF4 boundaries
sources.date_basis: Repository snapshot commit date; not the last modification date of each file.
supports: Default Python quantization uses FP32 midpoint selection and high-nibble-first packing.
Full zero blocks and partial zero blocks return different scales.
Default GEMM restores weights before the linear operation.
limitations: The Python default path is distinct from native CPU and CUDA execution.
CUDA NF4 thresholds do not prove eight-bit blockwise byte parity.

sources.title: Native CPU blockwise quantization
sources.date_basis: Repository snapshot commit date; not the last modification date of each file.
supports: Native CPU blockwise quantization rounds normalized values to a 65,536-entry lookup table.
Its zero blocks return code zero and scale zero.
limitations: Native CPU is not the default Python byte oracle. Neither native CPU nor CUDA executed in this research.

sources.title: Four-bit matrix multiplication and gradients
sources.date_basis: Repository snapshot commit date; not the last modification date of each file.
supports: MatMul4Bit restores weights for the input gradient and leaves the packed-weight gradient unset.
Nested GEMM supports second-level block size 256.
Gradient requirements select the autograd path.
limitations: Source inspection does not establish rank-three bias-gradient correctness or resumed training behavior.

sources.title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
supports: NF4 uses normal-distribution quantiles with an exact zero.
Double quantization compresses centered first-level scales.
QLoRA passes gradients through a frozen quantized base into trainable adapters.
limitations: The paper reports GPU experiments. It does not establish TPU results or current package byte behavior.

sources.title: 8-bit Optimizers via Block-wise Quantization
supports: Blockwise dynamic quantization uses independent scales and a nonlinear numerical map.
limitations: Optimizer experiments do not certify nested NF4 state, TensorImpl transfer, or TPU behavior.
